_readme: Converted from data/items.csv (CineFiles25/MMMM-TheRevolussionOfRenzoRenzi) and kept in sync with it: core navigation fields at the top level
(id, title, creator, images, externalLinks, texts, mapPosition), every other cataloguing field from the CSV preserved verbatim under 'metadata'.
16 items. images = local files in assets/items/. externalLinks = things hosted elsewhere (YouTube embeds, Bologna Fotografata, Archivio Luce);
'embedUrl' is set only where the provider allows embedding in an <iframe>.
mapPosition.area is a room id from 'rooms' below. mapPosition.x / .y are PERCENTAGES (0-100) of the width/height of
assets/img/museum/gallery_planimetry_no_punti.png (4032x3024) -- not pixels -- so they survive any display size. See map.html.
Positions come from Claudia's annotated sketch (final planimetry): one dot per item. Each text still holds only the CSV description;
the whimsical/academic versions are in data/text_grid.md and not imported yet. See ARCHITECTURE-NOTES.md for open questions.

items.title: L'armata s'agapò
items.creator: Renzo Renzi

metadata.subject: Italian occupation of Greece; antimilitarism; military justice; Cinema Nuovo; Renzo Renzi; Guido Aristarco
metadata.format: Manuscript draft and printed periodical article; digital surrogate available through the Cineteca di Bologna Renzo Renzi page
metadata.relation: Renzo Renzi Fund; Cinema Nuovo; From Arcadia to Peschiera. The s'agapò trial
metadata.physical_description: First manuscript version with corrections and cuts; printed article in Cinema Nuovo
metadata.current_location: Biblioteca Renzo Renzi. Cinema e Fotografia
metadata.depicted_place: Italian-occupied Greece; Peschiera del Garda prison; Italy
metadata.archival_description: Unit 3.2.1, Articles and letters for L'armata s'agapò, in the Renzo Renzi Fund inventory.
metadata.conditions_governing_access: Digital images are presented on the Cineteca di Bologna Renzo Renzi page; wider digitized materials are accessible from a dedicated library workstation.

texts.content: Article published in Cinema Nuovo no. 4 in February 1953. The text dealt with the Italian occupation of Greece and had a strong antimilitarist tone. Its publication led to charges of insulting the armed forces against Renzi and Guido Aristarco, their imprisonment in the military prison of Peschiera del Garda, and a public legal and cultural debate.
